description: Minimal Quartz Java project with two Job consumers (@DisallowConcurrentExecution on one), JobBuilder.newJob producers, TriggerBuilder.newTrigger, and scheduler.scheduleJob call sites. Used by the extraction-quality benchmark to verify PRODUCES/CONSUMES edge emission for Quartz Java.

expected_relationships.note: #6490 arm B. `public class AppScheduler { public void start() throws Exception }`.
Second top-level class in the same file; the CONTAINS must not be hoisted onto SendEmailJob.
The job-class view of the same declaration, emitted by the Quartz framework pass.

`public class SendEmailJob implements Job`. Java DOES emit this hierarchy edge — the C# Quartz.NET fixture's identical `class ReportJob : IJob` does not, which is the language-parity gap reported for csharp-quartz-net-mini.
`JobDetail emailJob = JobBuilder.newJob(SendEmailJob.class)…` — Quartz is external, so a bare-name target is correct.
`scheduler.scheduleJob(emailJob, emailTrigger);` resolved through the declared local type Scheduler.
`import org.quartz.*;` and the two static imports.

`JobBuilder.newJob(SendEmailJob.class).withIdentity("email-job", "email-group").build()` scheduled via scheduler.scheduleJob — the scheduled-job entity binds to the job class it runs. This is the one producer→consumer link the corpus actually emits for a scheduler.

#6490 arm B FINDING: AppScheduler.start schedules TWO jobs — `scheduler.scheduleJob(emailJob, emailTrigger)` and `scheduler.scheduleJob(reportJob, emailTrigger)` — and only SendEmailJob gets a SCOPE.ScheduledJob entity and a TRIGGERS edge. GenerateReportJob is built through the STATIC import `newJob(GenerateReportJob.class)` rather than `JobBuilder.newJob(...)`, and the scheduler pass does not recognise that form, so half the schedule is invisible. The entity row above pins the newJob<GenerateReportJob> producer, but nothing pinned the missing edge until now.

#6741 arm 2. `JobBuilder.newJob(SendEmailJob.class).withIdentity("email-job", …)` in AppScheduler.java dispatches a job class declared in jobs/SendEmailJob.java. internal/custom/java/quartz.go was the repo's only real PRODUCES emitter and paired producer to consumer within one PatternResult, i.e. same-file only, so it could never fire here. The producer now targets the resolvable `Class:<Name>` stub, which the resolver binds across files. ADR-0028 §1: the one-hop degenerate form (producer → job class, task:quartz:<Class> carried as a property) is the blessed shape where the pass mints no separate work-unit node.

#6741 arm 2. The static-import producer `newJob(GenerateReportJob.class)` reaches its OWN job class. Held constant against the row above: same file, same framework, same edge kind — the axis varied is the producer form (qualified JobBuilder.newJob vs static-import newJob) and, with it, the job class each must land on. A pairing that matched any job_class rather than the referenced one would cross these two rows and is what this pair pins. Note this is also the job the scheduled-jobs pass misses entirely (see the nice_to_have TRIGGERS row above) — PRODUCES is the only edge that reaches it.

#6490 arm B FINDING (identical to csharp-quartz-net-mini): the `scheduler.scheduleJob` schedule_job entity is asserted as a must-have ENTITY and is extracted, but no edge points at it — nothing contains it, nothing calls it, it triggers nothing. Same for `job:email-job` and `trigger:email-trigger`. Three of this fixture's producer entities are graph orphans.
